key_insight: Differentiable foundation models enable joint optimization of crystal composition and structure, yielding candidate photovoltaic absorbers near a target band gap.
engineering_relevance: This approach could accelerate solar-absorber screening by optimizing electronic properties alongside an energy-based stability penalty.
method: Extend pretrained EquiformerV3 to continuous species weights and site occupancies without fractional-data retraining.
Use property-model gradients and a learned energy penalty to update composition, atom count, positions, and lattice vectors.
Validate absorber candidates with SCAN calculations and assess finite-temperature phase competition.
evidence_signal: SCAN calculations confirm ten novel absorber structures with gaps within 20% of 1.34 eV on their respective raw or empirically corrected scales, all within 70 meV/atom of the DFT hull.
watch_item: Training-functional band-gap bias propagates into designs unless corrected in the objective; these computational candidates are not demonstrated solar cells.
paper_title: Inverse design of superconductors and semiconductors with differentiable foundation models
